chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

Whenever the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was brought wealth, he would place it in the treasury of the Muslims. Then he would gather those entitled to it. Then he would thrust his hand into the wealth and scatter it to the right and left, saying: O gold! O silver! Do not deceive me -- deceive someone else. This is my harvest and the best of it is in it, since every harvester brings his hand to his own mouth.

Then he would not leave until he had distributed everything in the treasury of the Muslims and given every person their due right. Then he would order it to be swept and sprinkled with water. Then he would pray two units of prayer in it. Then he would divorce the worldly life three times,
saying after the taslim: O worldly life! Do not present yourself to me, do not make me long for you, and do not deceive me, for I have divorced you three times with no return.

key_terms.بيت مال المسلمين: The Muslim treasury (bayt al-mal), the public fund for community wealth
key_terms.بيضاء: White one, a poetic term for silver coins (dirhams)
key_terms.صفراء: Yellow one, a poetic term for gold coins (dinars)
key_terms.طلقتك ثلاثا: I have divorced you three times -- an irrevocable divorce in Islamic law, used metaphorically for renouncing the world

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali distribute the Muslim treasury and what did he say about worldly wealth?
ai.summary: Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, a close companion of Imam Ali (AS), describes his habitual practice at the treasury. Whenever wealth was brought in, Ali would personally distribute every last coin to those entitled, addressing gold and silver coins directly, warning them not to tempt him. After emptying the treasury, he would have it swept and washed, pray two units of prayer inside it, and then declare a triple divorce from the worldly life -- a metaphor drawn from Islamic marital law meaning a final, irrevocable rejection. This narrative exemplifies the ascetic governance ideal of early Islam.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from Isma`il b. Marrar from Yunus b. `Abd al-Rahman from `Abdullah b. Sinan from Abi Hamza al-Thumali from al-Asbagh b. Nubata. He said:

Whenever Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) was given money, he put it in the treasury of the Muslims (bayt al-mal al-muslimin). Then, he would gather those who were wronged, and he would take the money with his hand and distribute it left and right while saying: O gold, O silver! Do not deceive me – deceive someone else. I give this to others and forbid my hand from it.

He would not leave until he distributed what was in the treasury of the Muslims and gave everyone their due right. Then, he would call for it to be swept and washed. Then, he would pray two units in it. Then, he would divorce this world three times;
saying after the taslim: O world! Do not present yourself to me, do not make me long for you, and do not deceive me, for I have divorced you three times, and there is no coming back to you.
